# Genesis Apocryphon Column 4 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 1QapGen (Cave 1), Col. 4 | **Condition:** Fragmentary; heavily damaged

---

**4:1** [...] So Methuselah set out [...] to find Enoch his father [...]

**4:2** [...] at the farthest reaches of the earth [...] in Parvaim [...]

**4:3** [...] and there he found him [...]

**4:4** [...] and he spoke to him [...]

**4:5** [...] all that his son Lamech had confided in him [...]

**4:6** [...] about the child [...]

**4:7** [...] he laid the whole story before him [...]

**4:8** [...] and he pressed him for the truth about this matter [...]

**4:9** [...] had the Watchers done this [...] or the holy ones [...]

**4:10** [...] or was Lamech truly the father [...]

**4:11** [...] then Enoch [...] gave his answer [...]

**4:12** [...] I know [...] the truth of it [...]

**4:13** [...]

**4:14** [...]

**4:15** [...]

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 4 brings Methuselah to the remote dwelling of Enoch at the edge of the world. The cosmic geography — the "ends of the earth" — evokes the visionary journeys described in 1 Enoch. The tension builds as Methuselah presents Lamech's desperate question to the one person in all creation who can answer it.*
